(CNN) — Investigators said Tuesday that they are pursuing several new leads in the case of a missing 5-year-old Florida girl who vanished a week ago and may have been abducted.

The Putnam County Sheriff’s Office searched the neighborhood of Haleigh Ann-Marie Cummings on Monday night, as well as surrounding areas. Authorities have said the girl may have been abducted, but officials declined to release details about the new leads.

“Those leads, like I said, are as a result of doing the neighborhood canvass last night, and we will be following up on those leads today,” said Capt. Steve Rose of the Putnam Sheriff’s Office.

Since the case was opened a week ago, authorities have received more than 1,200 tips about the missing girl, including 500 since Monday, Putnam County Sheriff Rick Ryan said.

On Tuesday afternoon, the sheriff’s office announced that it had revised the Amber Alert originally issued for the little girl, changing the description of her clothing.

“What we need people to focus on is the face, because we do not know at this time what the clothing was at this point,” said Dominick Pape with the Florida Department of Law Enforcement.

Rose said investigators also conducted a checkpoint in the area Monday night.

Ronald Cummings’ girlfriend, 17-year-old Misty Croslin, told police she was watching Haleigh when the child went missing sometime before dawn on February 10. Police are now questioning the sitter’s account.

Cummings shares his double-wide mobile home in Satsuma, east of Gainesville, with Croslin, his daughter Haleigh and his 4-year-old son. He has said that when he returned home at 3 a.m. ET, he was surprised to find Croslin awake and asked her why she was up.

Croslin waited until Cummings came home to call 911 about the girl’s disappearance, though authorities said it is unclear how long that wait was. Police said last week that Croslin had tucked Haleigh and her brother into bed at 8 p.m. before going to sleep at 10 p.m. The girl, her brother and Croslin usually sleep in the same bed.

Officials said they initially believed Haleigh may have wandered outside on her own, but they are now certain she was abducted.

Investigators are examining various aspects of the case, including trying to determine the whereabouts of 44 registered sex offenders who live within a 5-mile radius of the Cummings home, said Lt. Johnny Greenwood of the Putnam Sheriff’s Office.

A nationwide Amber Alert said the girl was last seen wearing a pink shirt and underwear.

**Disappearance of Florida 5-year-old remains one of Putnam County’s most haunting cases**

*SATSUMA, Florida* — Five-year-old **Haleigh Ann-Marie Cummings** vanished from her north Florida home in the early morning hours of February 10, 2009, setting off a massive search, an Amber Alert and a yearslong investigation that drew national attention but has never resulted in an arrest.

Haleigh was reported missing from a mobile home in Satsuma, an unincorporated community in Putnam County, where she had been staying with her father’s then-girlfriend, **Misty Croslin**, while her father, **Ronald Cummings**, was at work. Croslin told investigators she woke up and discovered Haleigh gone, with a back door ajar.

Within hours, law enforcement officers, volunteers and search teams began combing wooded areas, waterways and nearby neighborhoods. The case quickly expanded beyond Putnam County, with state and federal agencies assisting local investigators.

### Massive investigation and thousands of tips

Putnam County officials said the investigation generated **thousands of tips** from across Florida and around the country. Investigators followed leads involving possible sightings, family acquaintances, sex offenders, waterways and wooded terrain. Search teams used divers, cadaver dogs, helicopters and sonar equipment in an effort to find evidence.

Authorities repeatedly said they believed someone had information that could solve the case. Over time, however, leads dried up or failed to produce enough evidence for charges.

The Putnam County Sheriff’s Office has said publicly that Haleigh’s case remains open. Officials have also said investigators do not consider the disappearance a simple runaway case, given Haleigh’s age and the circumstances under which she vanished.

### Amber Alert and changes to Florida’s missing-child response

Haleigh’s disappearance also became part of a broader discussion in Florida about how quickly missing-child alerts are issued and how cases are classified.

An **Amber Alert** was issued after Haleigh was reported missing, spreading her description across highway signs, media broadcasts and law enforcement networks. The alert helped generate national attention and a flood of tips.

In the years after the case, Florida officials reviewed and refined missing-child notification procedures, including the use of alerts for cases that may not meet the strict criteria for an Amber Alert. State officials emphasized the need for faster information-sharing among local law enforcement, the Florida Department of Law Enforcement and the public when a child is believed to be in danger.

The case underscored a persistent challenge for investigators: Amber Alerts are powerful tools, but they require specific information, such as evidence of an abduction and descriptive details about a suspect or vehicle. When that information is limited, authorities may turn to other missing-child alerts and media outreach.

### Putnam County officials: Case remains open

Putnam County officials have said over the years that Haleigh’s disappearance remains an active investigation and that detectives continue to review tips when new information comes in.

Sheriff’s officials have described the case as one that deeply affected the community and the agency. Investigators have also said that changing statements and conflicting accounts complicated the case early on.

No one has been charged in connection with Haleigh’s disappearance.

Law enforcement officials continue to ask anyone with information — even details that may seem insignificant — to contact the **Putnam County Sheriff’s Office** or the **Florida Department of Law Enforcement**.

Haleigh was 5 years old when she disappeared. If alive today, she would be in her 20s.

**Investigators search neighborhoods, follow leads after 5-year-old Florida girl vanishes from mobile home**

**SATSUMA, Fla. (AP/CNN)** — Investigators fanned out across rural neighborhoods in northeast Florida, knocked on doors and followed up on a flood of tips after 5-year-old Haleigh Cummings disappeared from her father’s mobile home, authorities said.

Haleigh was reported missing early Tuesday from a residence in Satsuma, a small Putnam County community along the St. Johns River. The child’s father, Ronald Cummings, had returned home from work to find her gone, according to investigators. His girlfriend, who had been watching Haleigh and her younger brother, told authorities the girl was missing from her bed.

Putnam County sheriff’s officials said deputies, detectives, state law enforcement agents and volunteers searched the area around the home, including nearby roads, wooded lots, ditches, sheds and other properties. Authorities also canvassed surrounding neighborhoods, asking residents whether they had seen anything unusual overnight.

“We are following every lead that comes in,” the sheriff’s office said. “At this point, our priority is finding Haleigh and bringing her home.”

Investigators said the circumstances of the disappearance were suspicious. Authorities have not said whether they believe Haleigh wandered away or was taken, but search teams treated the case as urgent from the first hours because of her age and the overnight conditions.

The Florida Department of Law Enforcement and other agencies joined the investigation, and an Amber Alert was issued. Officials released Haleigh’s description and asked the public to report any information, no matter how minor it might seem.

Haleigh was described as a 5-year-old white girl, about 3 feet tall and weighing roughly 39 pounds, with blond hair and brown eyes. Authorities said she was last seen wearing a pink shirt.

Family members pleaded for her safe return as search crews moved through the area. Ronald Cummings said he wanted anyone with information to contact investigators immediately.

“Please bring my little girl home,” he told reporters.

The disappearance drew intense attention in Satsuma, where residents said they were shaken by the idea that a child could vanish from inside a home. Neighbors watched as patrol cars and search teams moved in and out of the area, while investigators questioned family members and others who had been near the residence.

Authorities said they were examining the home and surrounding property for evidence. Investigators also worked to establish a timeline of when Haleigh was last seen, who was at the home and what happened in the hours before the 911 call.

No arrests were immediately announced, and officials cautioned against speculation. They said the search would continue by ground and air as long as necessary, with investigators checking tips from the public and reviewing possible sightings.

Anyone with information was urged to call the Putnam County Sheriff’s Office or local law enforcement.
